messages.text: Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut

metadata.summary: Sober Glory turned the tables on Supreme Novices’ Hurdle conqueror Old Park Star to make a faultless chasing bow in the Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners’ Chase at Ffos Las.
metadata.content: Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut A dramatic afternoon at Ffos Las saw Sober Glory soar to success on chase debut for the Hobbs and White team with old rival Old Park Star fading into third with a broken blood vessel. Wednesday 18 November 2026 15:37, UK Image: Sober Glory ridden by Harry Cobden wins the William Hill Racing Epic Boosts Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) at Newbury Racecourse Sober Glory turned the tables on Supreme Novices’ Hurdle conqueror Old Park Star to make a faultless chasing bow in the Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners’ Chase at Ffos Las. One of the most eagerly-anticipated showdowns of the early season as the dry spell forced the exciting duo to west Wales, the main protagonists were immediately to the fore with Philip Hobbs and Johnson White's Sober Glory the more sure-footed of the duo in the early exchanges. There was little to separate the pair as a fine leap four out brought the Nico de Boinville-ridden Old Park Star alongside, but Ben Jones soon reclaimed the advantage in the home straight aboard the 5-4 second favourite. With the gap growing all the way up the home straight, the Cheltenham Festival runner-up gained revenge over Nicky Henderson's 4-5 favourite, sauntering to an impressive nine-and-a-half length opening victory over fences. messages.text: Zverev notified of lawsuit by ex-partner during ATP Finals

metadata.summary: World No 1 Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.
metadata.content: Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals Alexander Zverev has been notfied about a lawsuit filed by his ex-partner during ATP Finals; world No 1 advanced to the semi-finals of the season-ending tournament on Tuesday night Wednesday 18 November 2026 18:41, UK Image: Alexander Zverev has been notified of a lawsuit that has been filed against him by his former partner World No 1 Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday. The latest legal case brought by the mother of Zverev's former partner alleges the tennis player violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her. The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports news outlet L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven." Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.
